It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world that calls for a “truce” at the expense of the “spotless purity of truth,” and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the nature of church unity and ecumenical cooperation in this hour? [3, 1324, 1325, 1503, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the “noise and tumult” of divisions within the visible church, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that the “gates of hell” cannot win the “Truth War” against the only true Head of the church? [13, 20, 1193, 1324, 1395, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “common ground” with those who “turn the grace of our God into lewdness,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs His “chosen people” through a unity that is inseparable from sound doctrine [11, 28, 1303, 1420, 1503, 1542, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the scattering of the church under persecution is not an “administrative anomaly” but a means by which the Master “spreads the Word” while purifying His “vessels for honor” [15, 68, 361, 1030, 1143, 1532, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Foundation of True Unity**

**Verse**
“I, therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you to walk worthy of the calling with which you were called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace” (Ephesians 4:1–3). [58, 1225, 1461, Conversation History]. “There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus” (Galatians 3:28). [399, 1195, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that “biblical orthodoxy encompasses orthopraxy,” meaning that true unity is a “supernatural work of God” found only among those who “abide in My word” (John 8:31) [11, 1407, 1694, Conversation History]. We are “one bread and one body” because we all “partake of that one bread,” which is Christ Himself, the “only proper and legitimate Head of the church” (1 Corinthians 10:17) [1195, 1598, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition asserts that “the church is the assembly of the citizens of heaven,” and this unity is not based on “denominational spitting contests” but on a “shared commitment to biblical truth” (Philippians 3:20) [395, 589, 1465, Conversation History]. As the Lord Jesus prayed, His people are to be “one” so that “the world may believe that You sent Me” (John 17:21) [77, 1117, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “patchwork faith” that seeks unity through “ecumenical compromise,” for “can two walk together, unless they are agreed?” (Amos 3:3) [91, 1322, 1465, 1502, 1645, Conversation History]. Your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” by maintaining “the unity of the Spirit” with those who “call on the Lord from a pure heart,” refusing to “ape the world’s fads” for the sake of a “superficial unity” (2 Timothy 2:22; Titus 2:10) [11, 13, 101, 361, 1406, 1431, 1432, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious leaders” relied on “lineage and circumcision” to define their solidarity, often “despising” those of other nations (Acts 10:28; 11:3) [207, 1214, 1215, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that “God has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean,” for Christ has “broken down the middle wall of separation” to create “one new man from the two,” thus establishing a unity that transcends all “ethnic divisions” (Acts 10:28; Ephesians 2:14–15) [943, 1082, 1215, 1222, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Visible Church Under the Fire of Persecution**

**Verse**
“At that time a great persecution arose against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles... Therefore those who were scattered went everywhere preaching the word” (Acts 8:1, 4). [1030, 1197, Conversation History]. “ ‘Remember the word that I said to you, “A servant is not greater than his master.” If they persecuted Me, they will also persecute you’ ” (John 15:20). [53, 1056, 1316, 1513, 1672, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture handles the “noise and tumult” of persecution by revealing that the church is an “intangible and invisible” spiritual house that cannot be destroyed by “savage wolves” (Acts 20:29) [17, 458, 1415, 1425, Conversation History]. When the state “makes havoc of the church,” God “harnesses the deeds of the wicked” to ensure that “the Word of God is not chained” (2 Timothy 2:9) [25, 41, 1030, 1143, 1420, 1504, 1646, Conversation History]. The “record of history” shows that “all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution,” yet they are “protected by the power of God” (2 Timothy 3:12; 1 Peter 1:5) [74, 385, 442, 473, 1026, 1143, 1515, Conversation History]. The “church militant” remains “steadfast, immovable” because their King has “overcome the world” (John 16:33; 1 Corinthians 15:58) [131, 252, 1136, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that even in the “horrible pit” of suffering, the Lord “remains with them” and “perfects, confirms, strengthens and establishes” His people (1 Peter 5:10) [21, 94, 130, 136, 201, 1024, 1143, 1408, 1440, 1515, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” refusing to “lose heart” when you are “hated by all nations for My name’s sake,” for “he who endures to the end will be saved” (Matthew 24:9, 13; 1 Corinthians 9:27) [79, 116, 246, 252, 1026, 1055, 1406, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “national prosperity” and “dwelling in your land safely” were “temporal signs” of God’s favor (Leviticus 26:5) [409, 991, 1353, 1519, 1546, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this, revealing that the “true church” is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” who are “sojourners and pilgrims,” and their true “victory” is found in “the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony” rather than in physical safety (Revelation 12:11; 1 Peter 2:11) [13, 21, 26, 32, 92, 142, 440, 1313, 1402, 1426, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Cooperation and Contending for the Gospel**

**Verse**
“Beloved, while I was very diligent to write to you concerning our common salvation, I found it necessary to write to you exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints” (Jude 3). [760, 1137, 1141, 1246, 1358, 1389, 1440, 1463, Conversation History]. “If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into your house nor greet him; for he who greets him shares in his evil deeds” (2 John 10–11). [463, 766, 1356, 1466, 1496, 1554, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that “it is actually a sin not to fight when vital truths are under attack,” for the “spotless purity of truth” must always be at war with “the blackness of heresy” [1325, 1354, 1500, 1601, Conversation History]. Cooperation is “never appropriate” if it requires a “compromise” of essential doctrines like “justification by faith” and “substitutionary atonement” (Romans 3:24) [1429, 1430, 1490, 1653, Conversation History]. When “certain men have crept in unnoticed” to “deny the only Lord God,” the church must “examine everything carefully” and “refuse to yield submission” (Jude 4; 1 Thessalonians 5:21) [19, 120, 1313, 1316, 1442, 1480, 1503, 1515, 1529, 1720, Conversation History]. We are commanded to “mark those who cause divisions” and “avoid them,” for “no lie is of the truth” (Romans 16:17; 1 John 2:21) [1368, 1638, 1662, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “charitable dialogue” with apostates, but instead “wait for His Son from heaven” while you “shun” those who “speak perverse things” (Acts 20:30; 1 Thessalonians 1:10) [24, 51, 94, 123, 1286, 1408, 1415, 1428, 1466, 1503, 1515, 1672, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own,” and you must “be bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much conflict” (1 Thessalonians 2:2; 1 Corinthians 6:19) [12, 101, 212, 1138, 1160, 1262, 1406, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of Witness**
In the **ancient context**, “testifying in a dispute” required “two or three witnesses” to establish a “legal verdict” (Deuteronomy 17:6) [1294, 1317, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “witness,” showing that we are “ambassador-soldiers” who “conquer” through “righteous and allowable” activities, but primarily through a “wholesale transformation” of the mind that refuses to “exchange the truth of God for a lie” (Romans 1:25; 12:2) [11, 35, 163, 1301, 1387, 1390, 1406, 1503, 1532, 1662, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Triumph of the Unified Bride**

**Verse**
“ ‘Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.’ And to her it was granted to be arrayed in fine linen, clean and bright, for the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints” (Revelation 19:7–8). [939, 1210, Conversation History]. “Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!’ ” (Revelation 11:15). [103, 158, 1199, 1315, 1524, 1636, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of a divided and persecuted church by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 24, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. The “true church” will then be presented as a “glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle,” a “unified church, a body of saints for eternity” (Ephesians 5:27) [36, 1194, 1303, Conversation History]. On that Day, the “redeemed of the LORD” will be “registered in heaven” and find “perfect communion” in the “new Jerusalem” (Revelation 21:2; Hebrews 12:23) [943, 946, 1121, 1129, 1162, 1206, 1211, 1218, 1255, 1317, 1426, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting upon the “surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” His “unsearchable wisdom” will bring about the “final honoring of Jesus Christ” (Psalm 138:2; Daniel 7:14) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 201, 340, 351, 352, 412, 602, 957, 1132, 1143, 1306, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. “Wait for His Son from heaven,” for the “Lord, the righteous Judge,” will “wipe away every tear” and His “perfect kingdom” is “secure” (Revelation 21:4; 2 Timothy 4:8) [11, 24, 109, 412, 470, 719, 852, 948, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 324, 332, 361, 405, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: While we may cringe and actually voice displeasure when we hear someone taking God’s name in vain, we would do well to examine our own heart attitude. Indifference and lack of respect due His name from those who love Him may be just as heinous a sin. Unfortunately, it is this latter problem that often plagues Christianity. When believers have a low view of God, everything focuses on meeting felt needs within the body of Christ. When the church adopts such a perspective, it often offers people nothing more than spiritual placebos. It centers on psychology, self-esteem, entertainment, and a myriad of other diversions to attempt to meet perceived and felt needs.

Our Lord was about to start taking the lid off everything the Old Testament had kept shrouded in typology, symbolism, and prophetic hints. But the unveiling was purposely subtle, so that the only people who got it were authentic believers who were eager to learn the truth—those who had ears to hear. They understood the truths Jesus was teaching, not by some special clairvoyance or preternatural ability, but because they had enough interest to ask Jesus for the interpretation. To the rest, the mysteries remained cloaked in parabolic symbolism.

Not at all: “When he saw him, he had compassion” (Luke 10:33). What was Jesus trying to say? It was a preliminary answer to the original question. For these faithful believers, the name “Christian” was much more than just a general religious designation. It defined everything about them, including how they viewed both themselves and the world around them. The label underscored their love for a crucified Messiah along with their willingness to follow Him no matter the cost. It told of the wholesale transformation God had produced in their hearts, and witnessed to the fact that they had been made completely new in Him. They had died to their old way of life, having been born again into the family of God. Christian was not simply a title, but an entirely new way of thinking—one that had serious implications for how they lived—and ultimately how they died.

Submission to the lordship of Christ—a heart attitude that works itself out in obedience to Him—is the defining mark of those who are genuinely converted. First John 2:3 is explicit in this regard: “By this we know that we have come to know Him, if we keep His commandments.” As His slaves, we are expected “to obey Jesus Christ” (1 Peter 1:2), “to present [our] bodies a living and holy sacrifice, acceptable to God, which is [our] spiritual service of worship” (Rom. 12:1), and to “keep His commandments and do the things that are pleasing in His sight” (1 John 3:22). “You have been bought with a price,” Paul told the Corinthians, “therefore glorify God in your body” (1 Cor. 6:20). And later, “Whether, then, you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God” (10:31).

Slavery to Sin If anyone understood the horrors and abuses of the eighteenth-century slave trade, it was John Newton. He had experienced slavery from both sides— having lived as a slave in Africa, and having participated in the trade after returning home. As a minister, he had written about the abuses of slavery, and in the end, he was instrumental in bringing the British slave trade to its end. Christians today can rejoice in God’s providential use of John Newton —not only by saving him personally from his wicked past but also by using him (along with William Wilberforce and others) to end one of modern history’s great injustices.
